target_customer: Makers and small manufacturers using desktop FDM and SLA 3D printers who buy filament and resin
problem: Common desktop printing materials such as ABS and PLA trade off strength, shrinkage and ease of use. MadeSolid sold modified materials that aimed to combine them.
business_model: Hardware materials sales, filament and resin sold directly and through resellers such as MatterHackers

founders.name: Lance R. Pickens
education: University of Southern California, left the chemistry PhD program to start MadeSolid (per a 3DPrint.com style profile in search results, not opened)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2014-03-18) says the three co-founders have backgrounds in chemistry, nuclear engineering and business.

founders.name: Brian Martinez
prior_employers: Airbnb (global growth team, per YC page)
Atlas Project (Director of Growth, per YC page)
previous_startups: Air Angels, Airbnb alumni angel syndicate (launched, per YC page)

founders.name: David Rorex
founders.background_notes: YC lists him as Founder/CTO with no bio.

exit.reason: Cause and date of shutdown not public in anything found

competitors.name: ProtoPasta
competitors.what: Specialty composite filaments blending materials such as carbon fiber or iron into a plastic base
competitors.traction_then: Launched via a successful Kickstarter in late 2013 per search result summary

competitors.name: ABS and PLA filament makers (incumbent materials)
competitors.what: Standard desktop FDM materials that PET+ was positioned against
competitors.traction_then: Default materials for desktop printers such as MakerBot

technical_complexity.rationale: Formulating a modified PET filament and a lower viscosity SLA resin needed polymer chemistry expertise that most hobby suppliers lacked, though scale up was ordinary manufacturing.

defensibility.rationale: Formulation know how gave a short lead, but filaments were sold as commodities and many suppliers (ProtoPasta, ColorFabb launched 2013) were entering at once.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying by an incumbent was found. The company went inactive without a public explanation.

market_need_then: Desktop 3D printing was growing in 2013 and 2014 with MakerBot and Form 1 cited by TechCrunch as example printers, and users wanted materials with better properties than ABS or PLA. MadeSolid began as a printing service but found printer fail rates too high to run that at scale, per a search result summary.

branding.domain_note: madesolid.com is the exact match domain per the YC page. It now redirects to a parked style page (observed 2026).

identity.visual_style: Product line used descriptive suffix names such as FlexSolid, CastSolid and PET+

branding.brand_signature: The Solid suffix product family (FlexSolid, CastSolid)
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch, Make magazine and 3DPrint.com, sold through MatterHackers. No fan community or merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear, product descriptive name and trade press coverage, but no evidence of community pull beyond resellers.

pivots.why: Printer fail rates were too high for a service business, per a search result summary (source not opened)

outcome_analysis: MadeSolid sold PET+ filament, MS Resin and later FlexSolid and CastSolid from Emeryville after YC in Winter 2014, with a seed round reported in March 2014 and a Wefunder campaign that shows roughly 301 thousand dollars from 66 backers. YC lists it as inactive, but no shutdown notice, date or cause was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty. A commodity material market with many entrants is a plausible pressure but no source states it.
notes: Xconomy page could not be fetched (503); the March 26, 2014 seed with undisclosed amount comes from a search snippet and rests on a single outlet. Seedtable reports 423.3 thousand dollars across five rounds and Wellfound lists 10 investors including Plug and Play; the Wefunder amount and date are not separately dated, so round date is null. Seedtable also lists an 'other 2014' and 'other 2015' round not recorded individually. The company website redirect goes to a parked domain, so the site is effectively dead.
